name: Freelance transcriptionist / captioner (Rev)
summary: Transcribe or caption audio and video from Rev's work queue, paid per audio minute. Rev's help centre names Canada as an accepted location, but new applicants face a waitlist.
what_you_do: You pick audio or video files from Rev's online queue and type (or correct) what is said, following Rev's style guide; captioners also sync text to video. Pay is per minute of audio, so speed and accuracy determine what you earn per hour worked.
who_it_may_fit: You type fast and accurately, have a good ear for English, and can wait out an application queue for flexible piecework.
No degree or experience needed; you must be 18+ and physically located in an accepted country with ID from it
Choose your own hours and files; captioning and subtitle roles are listed at higher per-minute rates
who_it_may_not_fit: You need predictable income soon: there is a waitlist, pay is per audio minute (effective hourly pay is much lower than the headline), and no volume is guaranteed.
Unpaid quiz and transcription/caption sample (possibly a video) before approval; a rejected applicant reported a six-month wait before reapplying
Independent contractor with no benefits

eligibility_notes: Rev's freelancer help centre lists Canada among accepted locations (search summary; page not opened). Applicants must be physically located in an accepted area and hold official ID from it.

availability_evidence: rev.com/freelancers as indexed in October 2026: 'We currently have a waitlist due to high application volume. You can still apply.' No announcement of the waitlist ending was found.

other: Official identification from an accepted country

conditions_notes: Work is drawn from a shared queue after approval; no volume guarantee. v1 cited 2019 reporting of a pay-floor cut; not re-checked this pass.

advertised_rate.note: Rev freelancer pages (search-indexed): transcription $0.40–$1.10, captions $0.54–$1.10, subtitle translation $1.70–$4.00+ per audio/video minute. Older pages and reviews cite a $0.30 floor. Currency not shown in snippets (Rev is US-based).

unpaid_work: Unpaid English/grammar quiz plus a transcription or caption sample, possibly a video

risk_notes: Only accepted countries can apply; Rev support reportedly will not explain the country list.
contradictions: Lower pay bound: current freelancer pages say $0.40 per minute; older pages and third-party reviews say $0.30.

name: Freelance transcriptionist (short audio clips, TranscribeMe)
summary: Transcribe short audio clips on TranscribeMe's WorkHub after passing an entrance exam, paid per audio hour. In late August 2026 the exam was reported unavailable and recent reviews describe little or no work after onboarding.
what_you_do: After passing an entrance exam you log into WorkHub and transcribe short audio clips following TranscribeMe's style guide. Extra exams open specialty teams (e.g. legal, medical) that pay more.
who_it_may_fit: You want a low-commitment, text-only task you can do in short bursts and accept modest, uncertain pay.
Short clips suit small blocks of free time; only a computer and internet connection needed
who_it_may_not_fit: You need reliable earnings: advertised starting pay is $15–22 per audio hour, one audio hour can take two or more hours to transcribe, and 2026 reviews report no work after onboarding.
Unpaid entrance exam described as difficult, with no feedback on failure; one review found it unavailable in August 2026
Canada eligibility is only inferred from 'hires globally except California and Massachusetts' claims on third-party pages

conditions_notes: Reviews describe inconsistent volume; the company reportedly advertises average earnings of about $250 per month.

what_you_do: You build a profile with a photo and intro video, set your price and availability, and teach booked one-on-one lessons (English, French, other languages or subjects). Income depends on attracting and keeping students.
who_it_may_fit: You can teach a language (including French) or subject, enjoy live video teaching, and are willing to market yourself to build a student base.

Commission falls from 33% to 18% as your total taught hours grow
